learning_extracted: A readiness/vacuity gate can be stricter than the scoring criteria it exists to protect -- here, worst-cell-across-100%-of-seeds versus the run's own declared 60% seed_pass_fraction. Distinct failure mode from 'gate correctly catches a real substrate defect' (V3-EXQ-810); needs checking on every readiness precondition rather than assuming uniformity with the scoring logic in the same driver.

Comparing a flagged run against a sibling mint run on the identical substrate_hash (810a, started within 8 seconds of 834) is a fast, decisive way to rule out a substrate regression when a new driver's own readiness gate fails.

A baseline module's own docstring anticipating a specific failure mode (diversity-vs-repetition margin) is worth checking against the actual per-seed data before accepting a readiness gate's verdict at face value.
